title: Karlštejn Day Trip from Prague
short_description: Charles IV’s Gothic castle on its wooded hill, close to Prague. Door to door in your own Mercedes, with your chauffeur waiting at the foot of the village and one price for the whole car.
description:
Charles IV founded Karlštejn in 1348 as a place to keep the imperial regalia and his collection of holy relics. The castle rises in stages above the village: the Burgrave’s Palace, the Imperial Palace, the Marian Tower and, at the top, the Great Tower with the Chapel of the Holy Cross, its walls set with semi-precious stones.

The castle lies about 35 kilometres south-west of central Prague, so it is one of the easiest day trips from the city. It fits a morning or an afternoon, and it is a good first trip for guests with a short stay.

Cars cannot drive through Karlštejn village. Your chauffeur drops you at the closest point at the foot of the village, and from there you walk uphill on a paved lane lined with cafés and shops. In season a horse-drawn carriage runs part of the way, which you pay for on the spot. The chauffeur waits below and collects you at the same point.

Your chauffeur collects you at your address in Prague and the car waits for the time included in your booking, shown next to the price. You can add extra hours when you book. Time beyond your booking on the day is charged only after a person at Prestigo agrees to it.

The price is for the whole car, not per person. It covers the drive there and back, fuel, motorway tolls and your time at Karlštejn. You see the total before you pay.

Your chauffeur is a professional driver, not a guide. The castle can only be visited on a guided tour, which you book yourself, and entrance tickets are not included. We are glad to help you time the day around the tour slot you have booked.
highlights: A Gothic castle built by Emperor Charles IV to keep the crown jewels and holy relics
The Chapel of the Holy Cross in the Great Tower, with walls set with semi-precious stones
A walk up from the village on a paved lane lined with cafés and shops
The castle in its setting: a wooded hill above the valley of the Berounka
A short drive from Prague that fits a morning or an afternoon
A chauffeur waiting at the foot of the village while you visit

itinerary.title: Pickup at your Prague address
itinerary.body: Your chauffeur meets you at the door of your hotel or apartment in Prague at the time you chose. Match the start to your guided tour slot.

itinerary.title: Drive south-west to Karlštejn
itinerary.body: A short drive through the green valley of the Berounka brings you to the village below the castle.

itinerary.title: Drop-off at the foot of the village
itinerary.body: Cars cannot drive through the village. Your chauffeur drops you at the closest point and shows you where the car will wait.

itinerary.title: The walk up to the castle
itinerary.body: Walk uphill on the paved lane past the cafés and shops. If you would rather not walk all the way, a horse-drawn carriage usually runs part of the way in season; you pay for it on the spot.

itinerary.title: The castle tour
itinerary.body: Karlštejn is visited on a guided tour, which you book yourself. The tour takes you through the rooms of the castle, and some routes reach the Chapel of the Holy Cross.

itinerary.title: Coffee or lunch in the village
itinerary.body: On the way down, stop at one of the inns or cafés in the village. Then call or message your chauffeur; the car is waiting where you were dropped off.

itinerary.title: Return to your Prague address
itinerary.body: The same car and chauffeur bring you back to the same address in Prague where the day began.

includes: A private Mercedes with your own chauffeur, for your party only
Pickup and return at your address in Prague

excludes: The castle tour and entrance tickets, which you book yourself
A guide: your chauffeur drives and waits, but is not a guide
The horse-drawn carriage up from the village, paid on the spot
Extra hours beyond your booking, unless you add them when you book
pickup_info: Pickup and return are at your address in Prague: a hotel, an apartment or an office. Tell us the exact address when you book. Before the day you receive your chauffeur’s name and phone number, and on the day they wait at the door at the agreed time. At Karlštejn the car waits at the foot of the village, where you are dropped off.
important_info:
Karlštejn can only be visited on a guided tour. Book your tour in advance, and choose your start time to match it. The castle’s routes and opening seasons change through the year, so check before you travel.

Cars cannot drive through the village. Expect a walk uphill on a paved lane from where you are dropped off. Wear comfortable shoes.

In season a horse-drawn carriage may run part of the way up. It is paid separately and not always available.

There are cafés and inns in the village for coffee or lunch.

Your chauffeur drives and waits, but is not a guide. Entrance tickets and guided tours are not included.

faq.q: How is the price worked out?
faq.a: There is one price for the whole car, set for each car class. It covers the drive there and back, fuel, motorway tolls and the hours at the destination included in your booking. You can add extra hours when you book, and you see the total before you pay.

faq.q: Does the chauffeur wait and drive us back the same day?
faq.a: Yes. The same car and chauffeur take you to Karlštejn, wait for the time you booked and drive you back to your Prague address. Waiting during the hours in your booking is part of the price.

faq.q: Can the car drive up to the castle?
faq.a: No. Cars cannot drive through the village. Your chauffeur drops you at the closest point at the foot of the village, and you walk uphill or take a horse-drawn carriage in season. The carriage is paid separately.
No. Karlštejn can only be visited on a guided tour, which you book yourself. The price covers the car and the chauffeur, and the chauffeur does not act as a guide.

faq.q: What if we want to stay longer on the day?
faq.a: Tell your chauffeur. Time beyond your booking is charged only after a person at Prestigo agrees to it, at the same extra-hour price you saw when you booked. Nothing is charged automatically.

faq.q: How many people fit in one car?
faq.a: Up to three passengers in an E-Class or S-Class and up to six in a V-Class. Larger groups travel in two or more cars. Child seats are free in every class.
